utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see it at the time in 1994 when it was issued?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It's not 1992, it's 1994. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You did see this document at the time in 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I made a mistake. I first saw this document yesterday. What I meant was my contract with the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come to that. At the time that this document was issued in December 1994, what was the status of the 10th Sabotage Detachment? Was it fully formed or was the recruitment of new members still going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In October 1994, two platoons had been established. One belonged to Bijeljina, and the other one to Vlasenica. I think that in December the unit had been completed. The entire detachment was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And does this order about recruiting new members have anything to do with the completion of manning that unit in December 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document before. I cannot give an accurate answer to that question, but I think that by October 1994, the unit was complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look at the very top of the page, which says: "With a view to establishing and recruiting to the Main Staff VRS 10th Sabotage Detachment as the first VRS professional unit ..." Do you know what that means when General Mladic refers to the 10th Sabotage Detachment as the first VRS professional unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think it means that the Army of Republika Srpska would have its first professional unit that carried out tasks that had to do with going behind the lines of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we scroll down a little bit and just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you can quickly have a look at point 5.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And then go over to the next page. And in the very last part of point 7 it talks about: "... the Main Staff organisation and personnel sector shall prepare contracts and all other regulatory documents necessary to carry out this order." Now, did you receive a contract to do with your membership of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, I'd like to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P4487, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we now please look at 65 ter number 19906.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you recognise the document that we see on the screen, and if so, can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I recognise the document. This is my contract with the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page. Can you see your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the signature in the bottom right-hand corner, do you recognise whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There are two signatures in the lower right-hand corner. There's the signature of General Mladic and the commander of the detachment, Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go back now and -- to page 1 and just look at point 4. And point 4 says that the Main Staff: "Is obliged to pay Drazen Erdemovic, sergeant, an extra cash award for participation in any individual sabotage action according to the order by the authorised commanding officer." Is that what actually happened in practice when you went into a sabotage action? (redacted) Not in each and every action, because I think that Pelemis decided who would get a financial compensation and who could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, can you just look briefly at point 5, Mr. Erdemovic, where it says that the Main Staff: "Is obliged to ensure Drazen Erdemovic, sergeant, a priority in allocation of the apartment for his use through the competent authorities by the order of the president of RS." And my question for you, Mr. Erdemovic, is: At the time when you signed your contract, did you actually see a copy of the president's order that you be given a priority allocation of an apartment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4488, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd like to move to a different area now. In your Popovic testimony, this is at transcript page 10947, you described how Commander Pelemis ordered a member of your unit to slit the throat of a Muslim man in the town of Srebrenica. I'd like to show you a short piece of video and then ask you a couple of questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This is P4351.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If I can stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the centre of town in Srebrenica. That is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: For the record, we're looking at counter 50:9. Now, can we go back about 10 to 15 seconds, please. Okay. We're now at 41:9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you recognise what we can see in this still image?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the person that surrendered to the unit in Srebrenica. The commander of our unit ordered Zoran, nickname Maljic, to slit that person's throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is there anything particular about the body that -- that you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he had an American army jacket, and I remember that he had jeans, that he was wearing jeans.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did Pelemis say why he gave the order for this man to be killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall. No. No, he didn't say anything about why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you know why he was killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why he was killed. I could only assume then why he had been killed. Perhaps he was -- because he was of military age or -- I don't know. I cannot say, because Pelemis did not say why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Now after the attack on Srebrenica, you returned to Vlasenica on the 12th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the next day, on the 13th, you and some other members go to the funeral in Trebinje and then you're back in Vlasenica on the morning of the 15th.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This period when you went to the funeral in Trebinje, were you and the other members of your unit on leave?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, because when we went from Vlasenica to Trebinje, all the members were there in that house that belonged to our unit in Dragasevac. When we returned, I think most of the members of the Bijeljina platoon of our unit were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I want to show you a few photos now and ask you to mark some things on them with the help of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I first have Exhibit P4308. That's page 222 in e-court. It's 212 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's on this image?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the Branjevo Farm in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you mark the spot where your van parked when you arrived. If you can just put a number 1 at that spot.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Where was the office that the lieutenant-colonel went into?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you just put a number 2 next to the mark you made.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, can you draw a line or mark for us where the civilians walked -- I'll strike that. First can you mark the area where the buses parked with the civilians.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now can you mark the route that they walked to where they were shot.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And where was the area where they were shot at? Can you mark that with an X.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, if you can just put your initials down the bottom and today's date, in the bottom right-hand corner. Today is the 27th of February, 2012.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If this can be admitted, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4489, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Just one more question while we're looking at this image. Were the civilians escorted from the buses to the site where they were shot? Did any soldiers walk with them or near them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, initially Brano Gojkovic and Vlastimir Golijan escorted them from the bus to the site where they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we now go the same exhibit, P4308, page 225 in e-court. Page -- my apologies, page 235 in e-court, 225 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you recognise the building that's in this photo?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- in fact, I don't think. I know that is the cafe that we were in. It's across the road from the home in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to show the witness now a video that we ask for leave to add --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you hear the interpretation, Mr. Karadzic? Yes. No objection. Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 40587A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I just pause there. The counter is 11:18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, starting with the person on the left of the screen, not in the background but the three gentlemen standing in the foreground, do you recognise the one on the left?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: That's the commander of our unit, and General Krstic, and the person responsible for logistics in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Perhaps I could get you to mark this. If you could put a 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to capture the clip. I don't think it's possible to mark on the videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether we need marking. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just to make it very clear, the person in the middle is General Krstic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the person standing to the right of General Krstic on the left side of this -- the footage that we see, that's Commander Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the man with the moustache on the right-hand side is the logistics person?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has this been published in the e-court? We couldn't get the transcript. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's not part of our trial video, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to see the transcript on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We do have a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it has been published. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: No, it hasn't, but only because this was subtitled, but we can certainly publish the transcript as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We can keep playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please, 11:41.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you recall this ceremony where you were given an exceptional promotion to the rank of reserve infantry sergeant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We saw a few minutes ago on your contract that you signed in early 1995 that you were a sergeant. Can you explain how it is that here you're being promoted to the rank of sergeant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't explain that to you, because in that contract I was a sergeant, and then Pelemis stripped me of my rank because I didn't carry out the orders in the way that he wanted them to be carried out. And then the rank of sergeant was conferred upon me again, so I can't really explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And do you recall, just roughly, when were you stripped of your rank of sergeant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think it was in 1995, in February or March, something like that. Perhaps even earlier, but I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we keep playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We can stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this still shot? This is at counter 13:34.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see this very clearly on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Maybe we can play for another second and it may get a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that that is General Krstic in the right-hand corner, but the image is not very clear, so it's difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we play it back and play -- go back and play again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can stop there. Can we go back to where we were stopped previously?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is that any clearer now, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The only person I think it could be is General Krstic, but as for the others, I can't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And that's at 13:34. We can keep playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we move into private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And I'd like to tender that clip, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a second. We don't have to put it under seal? We can admit public --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I think the clip can be public. It was just the witness, what he talked about in private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: -- that needs to remain private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4490, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm about to move to a different area, so I'm not sure what the timing is today, but if it's convenient for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. How long would you need to conclude?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: A little while, maybe 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Better to take a break now. We'll have a break for an hour and resume at 1.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For this session we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis with Judge Lattanzi away due to her urgent personal matters. Yes. Please continue, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I want to move to a different topic now and ask you some questions about 1996. Did you travel to Serbia in the early part of that year?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you take any identification documents with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Were all of those documents in the name Drazen Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the other documents that you were carrying that were not in the name Drazen Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, it was an ID issued by the Bijeljina MUP, Republika Srpska ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: When did you get this other ID that was issued by the Bijeljina MUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it was issued in January or February 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, how were you told to go and get this identification? Was this something that you decided to do or something that someone else told you to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of our unit, Milorad Pelemis, said that we should go to the Bijeljina MUP and that we should take two photos with us and that we should be issued new documents under different names by the Bijeljina MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you actually go to Bijeljina, to the MUP there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what happened when you went there? Did you need to explain why you were there, or were they already expecting you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they knew why we were there. We just came to the lobby. We said that we were members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, and I can't recall now whether we had to fill out some forms and whether we had to sign off on that ID. I can't really recall, but I know that they knew why we were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it was not a leading question. You better leave it in the hands of Mr. Robinson. Yes, please continue, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, did 2nd Lieutenant Pelemis tell you why you needed to go and get new identification documents in a different name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. We were just ordered, me and several other Croats and a Muslim and a Slovene, that we should change our names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter 23463 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need to change to e-court from Sanction? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, this is an order from the Minister of the Interior, Dragan Kijac, to the head of the RS MUP public security. It's addressed to the VRS Main Staff Intelligence Administration for Information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And if we scroll down in both versions, and we move across to the left in English. Sorry, can we go back to the first page. And blow it up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, this order from Dragan Kijac encloses the text of a dispatch from the Main Staff intelligence administration from Colonel Petar Salapura. If you can just remind us who Colonel Petar Salapura is.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Petar Salapura was superior to our detachment's commander, Milorad Pelemis. He was a member of the intelligence department of the Main Staff of the VRS army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. And Colonel Salapura's dispatch says -- well, it's addressed to the minister personally and says: "Considering that we have a group of members in the 10th Sabotage Detachment who are foreign citizens or are on a list of individuals who have been indicted by The Hague Tribunal, we ask that you order the Bijeljina MUP to issue personal IDs with Serbian first and last names to these individuals, or with different first and last names for Serbian nationals. There are eight such individuals." And if we go over to the next page. It goes on and Colonel Salapura says: "Please inform us about your decision." And then we see Dragan Kijac with his order to the MUP saying: "You are required to ask on the request by the Main Staff of the VRS." Now, this refers to the issuing of identifications to eight members of the Sabotage Detachment. Can you remind us how many members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment were at Branjevo Farm on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were three, me, Marko Boskic, and Franc Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Erdemovic, how -- how many members of your unit were at the Branjevo Farm? Was it three or was it another number?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The way I heard your question when you asked me how many persons were supposed to be issued these new IDs, out of those eight persons there were only three of us. As for the Branjevo Farm, there were eight individuals there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And was this order issued at around the time when you received the order to go to Bijeljina and get a new identification?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Certainly. You testified a little while ago, just a few minutes ago, that you received your new identification in January or February 1996, and my question is just is this document at around the same time that you received your new identification?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This document is, as far as I can judge looking at the date, of January 16, 1996, but I can't recall exactly when it was that I received these new IDs, but I do know that it was in 1996, either in January or February.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: My last question on this document is: Can you see down there a stamp? It says "received" on "16 January 1996, at 1940 hours."

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And does -- in your experience as a soldier, would a stamp like this mean that that document had actually been sent or received somewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot claim really that I know, but if it is a stamp, it says that it was received and registered somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I tender that document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4491, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, after you arrived in Serbia, did you tell anyone about your involvement in the killings at Branjevo Farm and your knowledge about the killings at the Pilica cultural centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke with a former deputy commander of my unit, a one-time deputy commander of my unit. I can't recall his name as I sit here, but his last name was Kremenovic. I told him what had happened and what we had been ordered to do on that day. I told him that I could not reconcile with that. I explained what else was troubling me and the problems that I had in my own personal life, and we decided to get in touch with a journalist, a reporter for the ABC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you give an interview to that journalist?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And you told her your knowledge about the Branjevo Farm and the Pilica Dom in this interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Just very briefly, can you tell us what happened, after you gave that interview, in the next days and weeks.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Soon after that interview, Kremenovic and I were arrested by the state security of Serbia. Before we were arrested, when Kremenovic and I got home, this journalist called us and said that the bag containing the tape with my recorded interview had disappeared and that it was taken to the Belgrade airport. So we knew that we would soon be arrested. We tried to get in touch with the US embassy in Belgrade, but we weren't successful. After that, I can tell you what happened with me. I can't tell you anything about Kremenovic. We were taken -- I was taken to -- I was detained and taken to a Novi Sad detention facility. On the next day I was taken to court in Novi Sad, and from there, I was transferred by the state security to a house in Belgrade where I spent about a month, I believe, and then I was transferred to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to Exhibit P1490, page 47 in the English, and page 44 in the B/C/S. This is a notebook of General Ratko Mladic from the period 16 January 1996 to 28 November 1996. And then page 47 in English. That's it. And 44 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, these are General Mladic's notes of a conversation he had with President Karadzic on the 22nd of March, 1996, and I just have a couple of questions about this. We can see at the very top President Karadzic was recorded as saying: "A big show was put on for Albright. She expected they would find 1.200 Muslim bodies at Pilica, but they found some five bodies." What, in your view, was President Karadzic talking about when he referred to the 1.200 Muslim bodies at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is a reference to the interview that I gave to the ABC journalist, and also the statement that I gave to the Novi Sad court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, further down, in the third bullet point it says: "Fico was here last night, and he says that those two would sell the story about Srebrenica to The Hague." Do you have a view on who "those two" are being referenced in this sentence?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is a reference to me and Kremenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Was anyone else arrested with you in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, me and Radislav Kremenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit P3163. That's page 8 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This is an order issued by President Karadzic the day after that meeting we just looked at. It was issued on the 23rd of March, 1996. President Karadzic says in the first paragraph: "... in order to cast light on the facts regarding the discovery of a body in the Pilica area, I hereby order: "The Republika Srpska Army and the Main Staff and the Ministry of Interior shall immediately form a mixed expert commission of three members each to fully investigate and determine the facts regarding the alleged discovery of two decomposed bodies at the scene of earlier battles with the Muslim side in the Pilica area, Zvornik municipality." Mr. Erdemovic, I want to ask you in particular about the phrase "the scene of earlier battles with the Muslim side." Now, at any point in your statement to the journalist or your statement to the Serbian MUP, did you describe the events at Branjevo Farm as a battle or combat with the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And was this a battle or were you engaged in conflict with the Muslim men who were killed at Branjevo Farm on 16 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: May I please have 65 ter 4650 in e-court. This is a document from the 503rd Motorised Brigade command, security sector, on the 24th of December, 1998. Your Honours, we'll be leading evidence that the 503rd Motorised Brigade was the post-war replacement for the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, you have seen this document before; is that right? You were shown it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can just scroll slowly through the document. Go over to the next page. Next page in English, please. Under section 1.2, the author of this document indicates that he has learned information from various sources, and then that information is listed out over the next page and a half. If we can then go to the next page in English. A little bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about that bottom paragraph, which says: "Our assessment is that the SFOR will attempt to arrest some of the actual perpetrators in the Srebrenica case in order to make him, or them, a good witness. Please note that Erdemovic knows 'almost everything' and that many places and persons taking part in that are known to The Hague Tribunal." Mr. Erdemovic, do you have any comment on the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't mean to interrupt in mid question but I think I see where this is going. Mr. President, we would object to this as being irrelevant, a 1998 evaluation of this witness and his impact on the case two years after Dr. Karadzic has resigned as president. I don't see any relevance to this -- to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think a security assessment by the replacement to the Zvornik Brigade on the veracity of Mr. Erdemovic's statements and testimony is directly relevant to his credibility and the truthfulness of what he's been testifying about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, then in that case could I bring witnesses from other places to say, "We don't believe this witness," or "We don't believe any witness who comes to The Hague"? I don't think that's relevant whether somebody in the Zvornik Brigade successor believed retrospectively or retroactively or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber doubts that it's relevant to our case given that it is third party's assessment after the event. Why don't we move on, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I will. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The last area I want to ask you about, Mr. Erdemovic, is about another member of your unit called Dragan Todorovic. Do you know Mr. Dragan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I think that in -- at the time that I previously testified, I was asked about that person, but I can't really remember these things clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Was he at the Branjevo Farm on 16 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What about in the town of Pilica when you went to the cafe? Did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic testified in this case, and this is at transcript page 24214, and he said: "... Erdemovic also said that he was forced to do something at gunpoint. That's not true. Whoever would have made him do anything but at gunpoint would have had to answer for it later before the commander." Now, do you have any reaction to Mr. Todorovic's statement that you were not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic wasn't at the farm on that day. If he was in our unit, he should have been familiar with the order that was issued and that it's not that easy, in fact, to refuse to obey orders. He should have been aware of the consequences of refusing to abide by such orders. So I don't believe that Mr. Todorovic is speaking the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mitchell. Yes. Mr. Erdemovic, your evidence in the previous case was admitted in this case in lieu of your oral examination-in-chief, in addition to some supplemental questions by Mr. Mitchell. You will be now

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They didn't catch your "good day." Could you please remember to make a pause between question and answer, because otherwise the interpreters will have difficulty hearing us. I'll make the same effort. Thank you. Mr. Erdemovic, was the 10th Sabotage Detachment, the unit you were in, a group of criminals, or would one sooner say that in a certain sense this unit was elite one?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can only talk about the Bijeljina platoon. Up until the 16th of July, 1996 [as interpreted], when what happened on the farm happened, the tasks we carried out concerned infiltration and sabotage of warehouses and weapons that the ABiH had. On the 16th of July, 1996 [as interpreted], what happened at that farm? Well, I can't explain why those things happened. Why was the order issued to us to shoot those civilians on that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. President, but the date has been wrong twice now. If that could be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should read 1995, correct, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1995, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Up until that point in time it was an elite unit, a select unit. They acted nobly, and it was used to take action behind enemy lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just repeat what I have said. I'm a hundred per cent certain of these matters when it concerns the Bijeljina platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before that tragic date, the 16th of July, did you ever receive any instructions or orders that might have amounted to violations of international war law and the way that civilians should be treated? Up until that date had everything been done regularly and in accordance with international war law?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to shed some light on the situation in Srebrenica itself on the 10th and 11th of July. On the 10th of July, in the morning, you received a task -- rather, you were called to prepare to carry out a task. Were you told anything about the nature of the task, and did you prepare yourselves and take your equipment and, if so, how did you do this?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, we arrived at the barracks in Bijeljina. We had working hours. We would arrive at 8.00 in the morning. We would spend the time training in the barracks. That was the case on the 10th of July. However, on the 10th of July we were told we were going to carry out a task. We were to go home, first of all, and to take another uniform, our toiletries, and so on and so forth, and then we were to return to the barracks as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So at the time you weren't told where you were going, nor were you told what your task would be. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. In fact, yes, you are right. We weren't told where we were going to carry out this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that when you go to carry out a task it is only then that you are issued with weapons, ammunition, and other equipment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Whenever tasks were carried out, do you always have the same equipment, ammunition, weapons, or does this all depend on the task involved?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the whole, it was always the same, but sometimes we had explosives or weapons with silencers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the other equipment, would you sometimes be issued with sleeping bags or other types of equipment, and on the basis of the equipment issued to you, could you have a certain idea of where you were going and of the task you were going to carry out?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember having been issued with sleeping bags and so on, because we'd go behind enemy lines and then return as rapidly as possible so as not to be spotted. So we didn't spend much time on enemy territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as food is concerned, when were you issued with food, dry rations, and on the basis of the food issued to you, could you draw the conclusion as to whether you would be outside of urban areas, outside of our territory? What was the situation when it comes to food like?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, how can I explain this? I can't remember this exactly, but I think we were issued with normal rations of tinned food and food that could last for a long time, but if we were to spend a lengthier period of time somewhere, we would find ways of managing in the territory. We would find fruit and vegetables in the areas we spent time in. We never stayed behind enemy lines for very long, so we weren't too concerned about food.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you sometimes set off without being issued with any food?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I wouldn't want to say yes or no, because a lot of time has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 10th of July when you set off in the direction of Srebrenica, were you issued with any food?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, when -- what was the longest period of time for which you were provided with food?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Twenty-four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So how did you feed yourselves when you were in the Srebrenica area on the 10th and 11th of July? Did you have contact with some of the existing units, with their provisions, or were you autonomous when it comes to feeding yourselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karadzic, I really can't answer your question. I wouldn't want to answer by saying yes or no, because I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember whether you had dry rations and tins of food or did some neighbouring unit provide you with their catering facilities? Were you able to eat by having food provided by these other units?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, but if we had food, it was -- it consisted of dry rations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Erdemovic, you must be aware of this. Please put a pause between the question and answer. Yes. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that equipping a unit for a task involves a lot of work? You have to go home. You have to prepare yourself, take the necessary items. You have to be issued with certain items from the HQ, from the warehouse, and then when you return, all the work involved is considerable from a technical point of view?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was routine in our unit. We knew that prior to carrying out a task we had to be issued with weapons, and upon returning from a task we had to clean our weapons and return them to the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you spent the 11th -- the 10th and 11th in the Srebrenica area. There were no armed clashes, you were carrying out reconnaissance and securing "trasa." That's what one would say; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It's not quite true that we were carrying out reconnaissance, that Commander Pelemis said that our unit would move in the direction of the town on the 11th in the morning, and that because we didn't have enough men, we would be joined by a detachment from the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So on the 11th or the 12th in the morning you were told that you were no longer necessary; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you returned to your base in Vlasenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We returned to the base late in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it true that your colleague Mr. Koljivrat died in a traffic accident on the 12th when returning?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was anyone else killed or injured in that same accident?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A member of our unit from the Bijeljina platoon, Mladen. I can't remember his surname. He was injured, and the commander of our unit also sustained an injury to the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the 13th, you were given the task of joining an escort, escort the body, in fact, of Mr. Koljivrat to Trebinje. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How was the body of the deceased Koljivrat transported, and what means of transport did you use?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The late Koljivrat's body was in a refrigeration vehicle. I can't remember the kind of vehicle, and I and some other members from my unit were in a van.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So there was a van. There was one van, and all of you from that unit were in that van; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that Mr. Dragan Todorovic, who is mentioned here, was with you in that van?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 14th of July, you attended the funeral, isn't that correct? This was done in accordance with the prevailing customs with which you were familiar?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you returned. Did you stop over anywhere on that trip? Did you stop over anywhere between Trebinje and Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We stopped at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And tell me where, why, and for how long did you stop over there.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly where we stopped over, but we stopped over at Pale, because the commander of our unit, I think he told the driver of the van that we should stop over at Pale, and I can't remember the word in our language now. They wanted to pick up a metal detector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly from whom this was to be collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that you visited the family of a comrade of yours from the detachment? They had fled from Sarajevo and were living in some sort of a summer villa, some sort of summer house?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Srdjan Brijezo [phoen], does that name ring a bell? Did you manage to get some rest at his family home, and did you have breakfast there and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I cannot remember that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you arrive in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think we arrived in Vlasenica in the morning, on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Up until when -- or, rather, by when did you get to the base?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question. I didn't understand what you said. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. When did you arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember exactly. It was early in the morning on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During that day, the 15th, were you issued any equipment and weaponry, and did you leave Vlasenica and the base?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In order to leave the base after working hours, would you have to get a permit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sort of, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in order to leave the base after working hours, say, after 3.00, did you have to have a permit for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once you received permission to go into town, could you carry weapons when you went out in town, just for private business?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that we were allowed to be armed. However, some individuals from my unit had their personal weapons, pistols, and they had permits for that, if I can remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, please, to the best of your recollection, what was it that happened exactly on the 16th? What time did you get up on the morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th, in the morning, we got up and I cannot remember what time it was. Soon after that, Brano Gojkovic came and said to me, and Zoran Goronja, and Franc Kos, to take weapons and that we were going out on a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we be a bit more specific? When did you usually get up?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In Bijeljina, usually I got up around 7.00, and then I had an hour to get ready and go to barracks to be there by 8.00. I think that's the way it was, but I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you not spared a bit because of the trip? On the 16th of July, did you also show up at 8.00 or a bit later?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, we met in Dragasevac in Vlasenica, this house that we were in. That was the base of the Vlasenica platoon, so I didn't really have to go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have breakfast?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At what time did Brano Gojkovic arrive? After you got ready, after you had breakfast, when did he arrive, roughly?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but perhaps it was 9.00 in the morning or 10.00 in the morning. I think it was 9.00. I don't know. I cannot say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Brano Gojkovic tell you what kind of mission this was?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were you issued with that morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: An automatic rifle and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Nothing else?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the group as a whole? The eight of you from that unit, what were you issued with on that morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Weapons, ammunition, an 84 machine-gun and ammunition, and I cannot remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about food?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly. It must have been dry rations. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for this equipment that you were issued with, is a receipt issued and does it have to be signed? Your logistics man, does he have some kind of note stating what had been issued, and does somebody have to sign that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was a list, but that morning, I don't know whether anyone signed anything or who signed anything. I did not. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you report yourself? Did you volunteer? Did you say, "May I go," or were you told to do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As I have said a moment ago, Brano Gojkovic arrived, and that was the second floor in that house, and he said to me and to Goran and -- I mean, to Zoran Goronja and Franc Kos that we should get ready and that we would be going out on a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Only he and the two of you? Or were others told as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I know that we were up there in that room where the beds were, where we slept. I know about the three of us, and I don't know what happened to the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, then, how did you set out and how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We set out on our journey in a van. There were eight of us in this van.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that from Vlasenica you went westward towards Sekovici and then via Caparde to Zvornik? You took the longer road, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. From Dragasevac we went to Zvornik via Vlasenica. We did not go towards Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you sure of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. How far is it away from Dragasevac to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that, were you in the building of the military police, and did you stay there for about 20 minutes? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the military police building, but there were two military policemen there by the reception desk. Yes, we did not spend much time there in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly how long. Perhaps 20 minutes, perhaps half an hour. We didn't stay long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that point in time did you have any intentions of killing someone or doing anything that is forbidden?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, on the morning, on the 11th, before we went to Srebrenica, the commander of our unit, Milorad Pelemis, issued an order stating that civilians should not be touched, so I went by that order that civilians should not be touched, and I went by that on the 16th too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In other actions behind enemy lines, did you have only military targets, and were you supposed to take care of civilians then as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can talk about myself. I cannot talk about other members of my unit. I always tried not to hurt civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your commander like you on the basis of that instruction, and was this the climate that prevailed in your unit, that your only enemy was the military structure of the enemy?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I had a few problems with Mr. Pelemis and Mr. Salapura when in one action that I commanded, I explained that there would be major civilian losses. They told me that I was a liar, that I was lying, and from then onwards I started having problems with Mr. Pelemis. I cannot speak about other actions, because there were other groups that went out without me, so I don't know what their orders were and what they were told, but I know what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You told us that at the time of Srebrenica, your rank of sergeant had been taken away from you, that you had been stripped of that rank. Can you tell us when and why?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, in some orders -- or, rather, regarding some orders, I did not agree with Mr. Pelemis. Sometimes -- I mean, how do I explain this? He did not trust what I said very much, and he did not trust my views of the situation when I went out into actions. I cannot remember exactly when I was stripped of my rank, and I cannot even remember when this rank was given to me and why it was taken away from me, and I really cannot give you an accurate answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me remind you, when you testified in the Popovic case, on page 10963, you say -- I'm going to read it out in English now. Starting with line 7: "[In English] What was your rank or position at that time in the unit? "A. Before that I was corporal in the Army of Republika Srpska. I was a corporal in the 10th Sabotage Detachment, and because of conflict between me and Milorad Pelemis, who was the commander of our unit, he stripped me of the rank. I was actually commander of a group in the Bijeljina platoon, but at that moment I was just a regular soldier." [Interpretation] What you said in the Popovic case, was that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At some points in time and in some actions, you were the "komandir," commander of a group in the Bijeljina platoon; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. P4351. Could that please be shown to the witness briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, could you take a look at this. Do we agree that this is an order dated the 10th of July, 1995, and is that you under number 7, and does it say "vodnik," "sergeant," next to your name, and does it say "vojnik," "soldier" next to the next name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see the bottom of the page now to see who signed on behalf of Pelemis? Do you know whose signature this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I know it says "Milorad Pelemis" there, but I don't know whether that is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this signature say "Kos, Franc"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be more correct, then, to say that on the 10th of July, 1995, you were still a sergeant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before until testifying here, so I know what Pelemis decided, and now it says here that I'm a sergeant. Well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you first hear of this -- well, actually is it correct that as for the Branjevo Farm, that is the place where you first heard that someone should be killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear it in so many words that someone should be killed. What I heard was that buses with civilians from Srebrenica should be coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What time was that? In fact, first you arrived at that site; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At what time were you at the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly what the time was, but I think it was about 11.00, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived at the farm, you didn't see any prisoners or captives there; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How much time passed before the first bus arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not much time. I couldn't say exactly, but not much time passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did several buses arrive at once or did one bus arrive first? Was it only then followed by another one?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can remember the first bus arriving, and then the buses arrived one after another as far as I can remember. I don't know exactly, but the buses arrived one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the next bus arrive once the first one had left, or were there several buses at that place at the same time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think they arrived one by one. One bus followed the other. Perhaps two buses arrived in a very brief period of time at the same time. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if two buses arrived, would they both be at the site that you marked as a parking spot, or would one of them be there and the other somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember them being at the same site. If there was some other bus, I think it was at the parking spot on the road that led up to the farm, but I can't remember exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we're running out of time now, I would like to see P4490 in the e-court system, and then could we see 13347 or 6. P4490. If the Registrar can't find it, could the Prosecution please be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While waiting for that, Mr. Erdemovic, there was some lieutenant-colonel who was large, had noticeable traits. He was grey.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the image at 13:34:7, or 13:34:6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, P4490 is the video that we played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And we can play it from here if that would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please. That's what Mr. Karadzic wants probably. So that's why he indicated the time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We just need to know the times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He said 13:34:6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I thought it was 90 and not 09.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see this lieutenant-colonel in this image? Can you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I note that in this image, 13:34:5, 6, or 7, the witness isn't able to identify the lieutenant-colonel I have been referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you know that civilians were concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this removed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He didn't even identify there are lieutenant-colonels in this clip at all, did he? Do you see a lieutenant-colonel here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the question was whether I could see that lieutenant-colonel in this image, and I said that I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now I follow, yes. The only person you can identify is General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, how did you know that civilians were concerned? A minute ago you said they had no weapons. Do you think that after they had been captured someone would have taken them there with their weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As I have already said, Brano Gojkovic and the lieutenant-colonel said that they would arrive in buses, and this is how I drew my conclusion. All I am doing is repeating what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did you ever notice that in all three armies there were quite a few people who were fighting but they had no uniforms, and this was particularly the case in the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, I did see quite a few people without uniforms, but afterwards, after 1994 and 1995, I can't remember having seen many people who had no uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if you were at risk of being captured, God forbid, would you have got rid of your uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: If I went into action and if I was at risk of being captured, I think I would get rid of my uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Excellency, I see what the time is. Should I move on to another subject, or should I continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Mr. Erdemovic, you are aware of this rule, but please do not discuss with anybody else about your testimony. Tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of February, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
